# Public decks for growth-claim parser testing

Verified 4 October 2026. Ten decks from nine companies, verified as PDFs (four since converted, see below); GenesisAI appears in two distinct versions. PDF page counts and native text were checked from downloaded files, without OCR. Logos, photos and product screenshots are still images; the listed claim examples have native text. Page references below are one-based PDF page numbers.

The decks are included in `decks/`, with original URLs, publication evidence, page-by-page native-text counts and SHA-256 hashes in `manifest.json`. Six are the original PDFs, unedited. Four were converted from their PDFs: 01 and 03 to PowerPoint (`01-front-b.pptx`, `03-buffer.pptx`), 04 and 07 to Word (`04-clevergig.docx`, `07-equals-seed.docx`). For those four, the hashes and native-text counts in `manifest.json` describe the original PDF; slide and page numbers below match the converted files.

## Claim coverage

| Claim family | Verified examples | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Buffer p5: $150,000 annual revenue run rate; Moz p20: ~$10.8 million run rate; clevergig p6: EUR MRR and 15% MoM; zero2hero pp17/19: turnover and revenue forecast; GenesisAI 2024 p5: $8,000 revenue in 2022. Uber p20 has a hypothetical revenue scenario. | At least 5 decks have company revenue figures; distinguish historical figures from forecasts. |
| Retention | Front p13: 150% one-year and 120% six-month net retention; Buffer p7: 5% churn; Moz p21: ~25% churn in the first two paid months. clevergig pp6–7 adds customer MRR expansion in year two. | 3 explicit retention/churn decks, plus one expansion example. |
| Sales | Front pp12–13: LTV/CAC and ACV; Moz p20: ~$100 average paid acquisition cost; Buffer p7: up to $5 acquisition allowance per free user. | 3 decks. Buffer is an acquisition ceiling for free users, not paid-customer CAC. Sales cycle, win rate, pipeline, bookings and payback are not verified subtypes. |
| People | Moz p31: two-year team roadmap from 40 to 100; clevergig p11: Product/Growth teams to 20 by end-2020; zero2hero p22: six recruitment roles; Front pp10/14: sales staffing and headcount charts; Uber p25: hire a GM. | At least 3 decks. |
| Product dates | Buffer p6: January 2011 web launch and October 2011 API launch; Moz p2: February 2007 PRO launch and October 2008 Linkscape launch; TEA p11: Q3 2021 Preview 1 launch and later quarter-dated releases; Front pp19–20: 2018 API/app-store plans. | At least 3 decks, even without Front. These are historical decks, not current promises. |
| Market | clevergig p9: explicit EUR 200M ARR TAM; Uber p17: $4.2B annual taxi market; GenesisAI 2021 p11 and 2024 p4: total AI market forecasts; zero2hero pp7/11: category market sizes. | At least 3 decks for broad market sizing. Only clevergig has a verified literal TAM label; explicit SAM/SOM is a gap. |

## Other requirements and limits

| Requirement | Check |
|---|---|
| Public, intentional sharing | Founder releases/uploads for Front, Moz, Buffer, zero2hero, Uber and Equals; company-filed offering exhibits for both GenesisAI versions; a company homepage download link for TEA. clevergig has company-hosted public-event context, but no independent publication post was found. |
| No leaked/confidential deck | The set uses public releases. Front p23's “Confidential” label marks an undisclosed future product on the roadmap, not a restriction on the public deck; the founder explicitly released the redacted version. If the rule excludes any occurrence of that word, Front must be excluded and this becomes a 9-deck set. |
| Tech, seed through growth | Satisfied at the time of each pitch; not each company's current stage. SaaS/B2B predominates; Uber, zero2hero and TEA broaden the tech mix. GenesisAI versions are crowdfunding offerings rather than named venture rounds. |
| English; 10–40 pages; selectable text | All 10 PDFs are in English, range from 11 to 36 pages, and have native claim text. Image-only logos, photos and screenshots are not treated as extractable claim text. |
| Download without a paid account | All files were downloaded without a paid account. Front, Moz, Buffer and Uber use free mirrors of deliberately released originals. SEC can reject automated downloads; TEA has an expired website certificate. The supplied copies remove those practical dependencies. |
| Different numerical notation | Buffer p6: $3.6M; clevergig pp6/11: EUR 15K / EUR 5M; Uber p3: $500k; Front p13: 4.9x and 120%; Moz p20: 13,500. Equivalent notation families are covered. Exact literal EUR 1.2M, 3x and 1,200 were not verified. |
| At least two currencies | USD in Buffer/Moz/Uber/GenesisAI; EUR in clevergig; GBP in zero2hero. |
| At least two decks with table claims | Front p12: quarterly spend/revenue and LTV/CAC table; zero2hero p19: financial projections table. Both were checked visually, with native values verified. |
| Chart-only claims with text labels | zero2hero p17: turnover series £49,284, £181,193, £278,085, £415,107 and £550,508 appear as chart data labels, not duplicated as a prose list/table of that same series. Its p19 financial table contains a different series. Native label extraction succeeds. If the requirement means an entire deck with all claims only in charts, that stricter requirement is not met. |
| Low-number control | Equals: most pages are qualitative. Its founders' previous Intercom ARR and team history must not be attributed to Equals. It still contains fundraising and runway figures, so it is a sparse control, not a zero-number document. |
| Reach two PPTX and two DOCX | Converted: Front and Buffer to PPTX, clevergig and Equals to DOCX, with editable text. The set is 6 PDF, 2 PPTX and 2 DOCX. |

Parser interpretation matters: market CAGR is not company revenue growth; funds raised are not revenue; commission percentage is not realized revenue; user growth is not revenue growth; token allocation is not headcount. zero2hero's chart and projection table contain inconsistent-looking figures: keep them as source claims rather than reconciling them into invented facts.
